title: Relief Valve
subtitle: A quiet smash toy
tagline: A quiet smash toy. Soft light, one thumb, no scores.
summary: Tap Crush and watch the press come down. No timer, no combo, no homework. A low-stimulation loop for when you just want something gentle to press. Play it on your phone.
why: Some nights a smash loop is a kinder door than a to-do list. Crush it as many times as you want.

title: Why Some Writing Sounds Like Talking
subtitle: Prosodic Cognitive Simulation
tagline: Same scene, four stops vs one held sentence. Feel why silent reading sounds like a voice.
summary: Four interactive labs on the mechanisms that keep an inner ear mid-breath: buffer resets, prosodic rhythm, delayed closure, and predictive syntax. Nitish Chauhan built this as a playful writing science toy, not a textbook.
why: Good prose is not just meaning. It is cadence. These labs make the phonological loop tangible so writers can stop accidentally resetting the reader every sentence.

title: Mental Models Reality Engine

tagline: Flip what the brain expects against what the math says, until the gap is hard to unsee.
summary: Nitish Chauhan's current priority interactive: Assumption Stacks, Compound Effect, and Pareto Gravity as a Labs Reality Engine. Companion write-up and ten-model Cognitive Rewiring sim live in the Library.
why: Self-help phrasing hides geometric reality. Cold statistical flips make mental models useful instead of decorative.
sourceFiles: Library: Final - Mental Models Visceral Math.md

title: Atlas / Bubble Chat
subtitle: A thinking workspace, not another AI messenger
tagline: Sessions, floating bubbles, and compression that makes knowledge denser - not longer.
summary: Atlas (working product name in the specs; Bubble Chat in the feature notes) rejects the single scrolling transcript. Conversation Mode keeps structured branches; Workspace Mode is a Figma-like canvas of Objects - chat, PDF, browser, notes, whiteboard - inside a Session. Closing Primary closes the Session; Replay restores layout like walking back into your desk. MVP roadmap: fork OpenMLC/HF Chat UI → canvas + spawn → bubble polish → cross-bubble drag → export/search. Core constraint from every Cursor brief: responsiveness over feature count; feel like index cards, not heavyweight windows.
why: Most AI clients are messaging apps. Nitish Chauhan's ADHD-shaped workflow needs parallel thoughts without losing the session narrative - spawn, park, pin-to-main, then compress.
principles: The computer organizes; the human thinks
modules: AI workers (Historian, Scout, Compression) isolated from chat UI
Export: folder of .md + session.json + questions archive
Compression pipeline: daily → weekly → monthly → yearly
mvpPhases: Canvas: drag, zoom, 60 FPS, Cmd+N spawn, layout persistence
Bubble polish: colors, titles, scroll memory, minimap
Interactions: shared clipboard, Pin-to-Main, Opt+Enter spawn

title: Vault
subtitle: Universal conversation capture that closes the mental loop
tagline: Capture everything accurately. Interpretation is optional. Capture is mandatory.
summary: Vault is an export-first Chrome extension (PRD + Engineering Spec V1). Finish a conversation on ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Grok, Perplexity, Cursor, or a generic page → Add to Queue → multi-select → export Markdown, JSON, HTML, plain text, or ZIP with assets. Sidebar is a temporary workspace, not permanent storage. No AI summaries, embeddings, RAG, or auto-tagging in V1 - those belong later, and never block capture. Guiding test: does this help capture and close the loop, or turn Vault into another knowledge management system?
why: Tabs stay open because people fear losing ideas. Manual copy-paste is slow and lossy. Vault's job is cognitive closure, not becoming a second brain.
principles: Capture first - never summarize or rewrite on the way out
User control - the extension never decides what matters
Low cognitive load - minimal clicks, no unnecessary prompts
Universal support - modular extractors + generic webpage fallback
Modular architecture - site-specific logic stays in extractors/
successCriteria: Reliable capture from supported AI sites
New user understands UI within ~one minute
Fewer tabs left open out of fear

title: Memory Capture Extension
subtitle: Phase 1 zero-friction Markdown capture for Cursor execution
tagline: A perfect screwdriver - not a Swiss Army knife. Capture is immediate, headless, and silent.
summary: Implementation guide optimized for Cursor: Manifest V3 background worker + content scripts + Turndown. Three modes (entire page, selection, link); silent chrome.downloads to Memory/Inbox/YYYY/MM/DD/title.md; fixed metadata template; duplicate detection via URL+content hash; Friction Counter (Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+F) logging friction notes to Memory/Friction/log.csv. ChatGPT/Claude DOM heuristics with Readability-style generic fallback. Offline-first - no cloud APIs in Phase 1. Coded under NitishLabs active-projects/memory-capture-extension; sits upstream of the fuller Vault product.
why: Organize later. At the moment of discovery, any decision (folder, tag, rename) is friction. Inbox-first is the whole point.
principles: If removing a feature doesn't make the product worse, it is not MVP

title: Hermes Agent Stack
subtitle: Middleware brain on the VPS; Telegram + WebUI as faces
tagline: Open WebUI is an interface. Hermes is the middleware. Pick the face; keep the brain.
summary: Self-hosted Hermes on the Nitish Chauhan VPS: systemd gateway, Telegram bot (@OGHermes_1bot) via webhook, WebUI at chat.nitishchauhan.com. Stack thinking from the lab notes: Hermes owns the agentic loop, tools, and memory; a ChatGPT-style WebUI (or Telegram) is just how you talk to it. Related design work: Historian-style day narrative, question-preserving compression, ADHD "collect the toys" capture agents - all plug into the same middleware once the runtime is solid.
why: Phone-first control without giving up a real agent (tools, memory, persistence). Portfolio stays on the main domain; cloud and chat live on their own subdomains.

architecture.brain: Hermes - agent loop, tools, memory, OpenAI-compatible API
adjacent: Optional Open WebUI as alternate face

liveNotes: Webhook preferred over long polling on the VPS
WebUI service on loopback; nginx terminates TLS
